clue.text: Bug home connected to separatist group

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a sect is a group that has broken away from a larger body

explanation.surface: Someone's house has been wired for surveillance by a breakaway faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' reads as a listening device in the surface, but it is the creature. IN for 'home' is the sense in 'staying in tonight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bug is an everyday informal word for any small creepy-crawly with six legs.

clue.text: Very upset? That's how the cookie crumbles

definitions.meaning: first meaning: emotionally shattered, a British informal phrase
second meaning, taken literally: a crumbling biscuit ends up in small pieces

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs distress with a shrug of resignation; the second half is read literally, describing the physical state of a broken cookie. 'In bits' is British slang for distraught.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means emotionally devastated in British slang, and literally describes something broken into many small fragments.

clue.text: Earnest revelling in our misdeeds

indicators.note: revelling is wild partying, so the letters that follow are thrown about riotously

parts.note: thirteen letters taken as written to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Earnest gleefully enjoys the wrongs we have done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earnest' looks like a man's name (Ernest) doing the revelling, but it is the definition; 'in' belongs to the letters to be rearranged, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest describes a person who is sincere and grave in intent, the same as one with a solemn, thoughtful disposition.

clue.text: Become ruder about rowers after loss in fifth place

indicators.note: a loss at a stated position means the letter standing there is dropped

parts.note: C is the abbreviation of circa, Latin for about
people who row a boat

explanation.surface: Someone grows more insulting about a rowing crew after it finishes fifth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fifth place' sounds like a race result for the crew, but it points to the fifth letter of OARSMEN, the M, which goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To coarsen is to grow cruder or less refined in manner, which is becoming ruder.

clue.text: Cries horribly when pierced by tip of little bladed implement

indicators.note: something pierced has another thing driven inside it
doing something horribly means doing it badly, so the letters come out mangled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its very first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone screams in pain when stabbed by a small knife.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged CRIES gives SICER, which opens after its first letter to take the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A slicer is a tool with a blade used for cutting food into thin pieces.

clue.text: Memorise last bit of carol on organ before November

indicators.note: the final bit of a word is its closing letter

parts.note: the closing letter of the word
the ear is the organ of hearing
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A singer commits the end of a Christmas carol to memory, played on a church organ before the festive season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the church instrument for the carol, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To memorise something is to learn it by heart, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Visits we heard couple eventually accepts

parts.note: a phrasal verb for dropping in on someone at their home

indicators.note: what we heard is what was spoken, so a word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a couple is two, which is said the same way as this short word

explanation.surface: A pair keeps calling on us until they finally win our approval.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the couple are the visitors, but 'couple' is just the number two, heard as TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To come around to an idea is to be gradually persuaded and finally agree with it.

clue.text: Maybe rat's lair surrounded by rubbish

indicators.note: to be surrounded is to sit inside something else

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
a den is an animal's hiding place

explanation.surface: A rat's nest sits in the middle of a pile of garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' reads as literal trash around the nest, but it means nonsense. 'Maybe' signals that a rat is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is one example of a gnawing mammal with continuously growing incisors.

clue.text: Organised rebrand for turkey farmer Matthews, say

indicators.note: to organise is to put things into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A marketing makeover is arranged for a famous poultry business.
explanation.walkthrough: Bernard Matthews was a British turkey farmer whose name became a well-known frozen-food brand; 'say' marks his first name as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The given name of the famous Norfolk poultry businessman is one example of someone bearing this first name.

clue.text: Not totally justified, evil men threaten mischief

indicators.note: taking only part of a run of words means the solution sits inside them

parts.note: runs from the final letter of the first word to the opening letter of the last

explanation.surface: A complaint that wicked men's threats are only partly warranted.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans four words, ignoring the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilment is playful or reckless wrongdoing, which is a synonym for mischief.

clue.text: Planned article by this writer written in papers

parts.note: the indefinite article

indicators.note: writing in something places it inside

parts.note: ID is identity papers
the setter referring to themselves

explanation.surface: A journalist's piece was scheduled for the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Papers' sounds like newspapers for the article, but it means identity documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aimed is intended or targeted, so it was planned with a goal in view.

clue.text: Overly large and small instruments

parts.note: too means excessively
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A range of musical instruments, some oversized and some tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instruments' suggests music, but it means implements; L and S come from garment size labels.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruments in the sense of implements for doing work are a standard synonym for these devices.

clue.text: Game against bridge opponents is not off

parts.note: V is versus, against
in bridge East and North sit on opposing sides
taken as written
the opposite of off

explanation.surface: A card game against rival bridge players is still going ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like the contest but it is the definition: meat from hunted animals. Bridge players are labelled by compass points, and East and North are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Game means wild animals hunted for food, and deer meat is a classic example.

clue.text: Told lad loudly to set down bright plant

indicators.note: what is told is spoken, so the next word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a lad is a son, which is pronounced like the star
F is forte, the musical direction to play loudly
to lower is to set something down

explanation.surface: A boy is shouted at to put down a shiny potted plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loudly' looks like part of the telling, but it is F, from music notation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall plant with large yellow-petalled heads, famously brilliant in colour and turning toward daylight.

clue.text: Cleaning part of leg in movement from side to side

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is held inside it

parts.note: a wag is a side-to-side shake, as of a tail
the front of the lower leg

explanation.surface: Scrubbing a leg with a back-and-forth motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement from side to side' sounds like a scrubbing action, but it is a dog's tail motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing and cleaning are synonyms for removing dirt, as nouns or verb forms.

clue.text: Struggle climbing iron defensive structure

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a fort is a fortified building

explanation.surface: A hard climb up an iron fortification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggle climbing' reads as a laborious ascent, but 'climbing' only flips the iron symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A struggle is a strenuous attempt, and exertion of energy is what effort names.

clue.text: Mean banks abandoning Japanese video game company

indicators.note: the banks are the edges of a word, and abandoning them drops its outer letters

parts.note: the maker of Mario and the Switch console

explanation.surface: Stingy banks pull out of funding a Japanese games firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' sits next to 'banks' as if describing stingy lenders, but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to have it as your purpose or plan.

clue.text: Grief at destroyed naval vessel

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Mourning over a warship that has been sunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyed' fits the surface as a sunk ship, and a destroyer is also a warship, which helps hide its role.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a type of warship used by navies for escort and patrol.

clue.text: Concur, taking part in beer games after reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, back to front
taking part means taking only a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: a run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Agreeing to join in drinking games after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After reflection' sounds like careful thought, but it means read the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to share the same opinion, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Contemptuously reject inducement close to corruption

parts.note: a spur is an incentive

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Scornfully turning down a bribe that verges on corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as 'nearly', but it means the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn is to refuse something with disdain, rejecting it scornfully.

clue.text: Stranger bringing Communist Party to the West

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: red is the colour of communism
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: An outsider introduces the Communist Party to Western countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stranger' looks like a noun for a newcomer but is the comparative adjective, and 'Party' is a social do, not a political one.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranger as a comparative adjective means more unusual, the same as more peculiar or weird.

clue.text: Turn from far side of embankment and pass water

indicators.note: the far side of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word
widdle is British childish slang for urinate

explanation.surface: Someone walks away from a riverside embankment to relieve themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass water' suggests crossing a river beside the embankment, but it means urinate; widdle is a childish British word for that.
explanation.definitionFit: To twiddle a knob or dial is to rotate it idly with the fingers.

clue.text: Time one stops working and clears up

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
I is the Roman numeral one
a machine that dies stops working

explanation.surface: At knocking-off time a worker downs tools and puts things in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One stops working' reads as a person clocking off, but 'one' is I and the stopping is a machine dying.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear up a room is to put it in order, which is exactly what someone does who tidies.

clue.text: Ancient mangles oiled at regular intervals

indicators.note: regular intervals means taking every other letter in turn

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: An old wringer for laundry is greased now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: A mangle is an old wringer with rollers for pressing water out of washing, which fits the antique surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient and age-old both describe something that has existed for a very long time.
